releases.title: VisionX on your Home Screen

highlights.title: A real widget
highlights.text: Add VisionX to your Home Screen: the live session, or your last one with its triggers and summary.

highlights.title: Lock Screen too
highlights.text: Small, medium, large and three Lock Screen sizes, with the VisionX eye and name.

highlights.title: No more errors
highlights.text: The widget no longer shows Scriptable's error text; it works offline and never shows photos.

changes: New Home Screen and Lock Screen widget in the shared frame (app-blueprints · widgets 1.0.0): logo tile, name, one hero, rows and a footer on the VisionX ground
While a session runs, the widget shows ● Live, the preset, the interval and the photos so far; otherwise the last session with the shortcuts that ran and its ✦ summary
A widget run no longer starts the app, so it can't fail with "Presenting a configured web view is not supported"
Settings › Widget: how often to ask iOS to refresh, and when to mark the widget out of date
Settings › Built with lists the widgets blueprint

releases.title: More room while you capture

highlights.title: Cleaner header
highlights.text: Tabs and the status line hide while a session runs and return when it stops.

highlights.title: Photos stay in view
highlights.text: The live, analyzing and analyzed photos stay pinned at the top as you scroll.

highlights.title: Half size on scroll
highlights.text: Scroll down and the photo row shrinks to half its height; scroll up and it grows back.

changes: While a session runs (or is paused), the tabs and status line are hidden; they come back when it stops
The photo row (Live, Analyzing, Analyzed) sticks under the header
Scrolling down shrinks the row to half its height, hides its captions and adds a shadow; scrolling back to the top restores it

releases.title: Launch screen, now shared

highlights.title: Same launch screen
highlights.text: The eye still draws itself and the tagline appears; nothing changes for you.

highlights.title: A shared blueprint
highlights.text: The launch screen is now the launch-screen blueprint, shared by all the apps.

highlights.title: Built with
highlights.text: Settings › Built with lists the Launch screen blueprint.

changes: Launch screen code aligned with the shared launch-screen blueprint 1.0.0 (generic part names, colour variables, script first in the page)
Blueprint trace: BLUEPRINTS block, Settings › Built with and docs/BLUEPRINTS.md list launch-screen 1.0.0

releases.title: Sees. Understands. Acts.

highlights.title: A logo of its own
highlights.text: The watching eye: a red record-dot pupil and a teal scan line.

highlights.title: Launch screen
highlights.text: The eye draws itself and the tagline appears for about 2 seconds; tap to skip.

highlights.title: Branded everywhere
highlights.text: The logo sits in the header, on the idle Live tab and in the README.

changes: New VisionX logo (watching eye): docs/logo.svg and a 1024 px app icon, docs/icon-1024.png
Launch screen shown for 2.4 s with a short animation and the tagline "Sees. Understands. Acts."; tap to skip; still with Reduce Motion
Logo mark in the sticky header, the logo on the Live tab when no session runs, and at the top of the README

releases.title: Pick shortcuts, copy triggers

highlights.title: Pick from your shortcuts
highlights.text: Load your shortcut list once, then choose instead of typing exact names.

highlights.title: Duplicate a trigger
highlights.text: Copy a trigger in one tap, then just change the shortcut.

highlights.title: Suggestions as you type
highlights.text: Every shortcut name field suggests matching shortcuts.

changes: Load my shortcuts in the trigger form reads all your shortcut names through a small helper shortcut, VisionX Shortcut List
Choose a shortcut from a picker above the name field; the list is remembered and can be reloaded
Shortcut name fields for triggers, Apple Intelligence and the checker suggest matching names as you type
Step-by-step setup for the helper shortcut, opened automatically if loading fails
Duplicate in the trigger form saves a copy of the trigger as shown, right after the original, and opens it for editing

releases.title: Charts you can actually see

highlights.title: Real charts in summaries
highlights.text: Pie, bar and line charts from the AI now draw as graphics, not code.

highlights.title: Make it visual
highlights.text: One tap rewrites your instructions so results come back as charts and tiles.

highlights.title: Headline number tiles
highlights.text: Key counts show as big, easy-to-read tiles at the top of the summary.

changes: Mermaid pie blocks draw as a donut with a legend of counts and shares
Mermaid xychart-beta blocks draw as horizontal bars and/or a line chart
New stats blocks draw as headline number tiles with an optional note
"Make it visual" button next to Refine with AI and in the instructions editor
The model is told exactly which visuals the app can draw, so it uses the right syntax
Charts use the selected palette and work offline; anything that doesn't parse stays a code block
fixes: The Session ended sheet shows the summary formatted, instead of raw Markdown

releases.title: Live, analyzing, analyzed: one row

highlights.title: Three photos, one row
highlights.text: Live camera, the photo being analyzed and the last analyzed one, side by side.

highlights.title: Clearly in the summary
highlights.text: The last analyzed photo is outlined and marked "In the summary".

highlights.title: Zoom buttons on the preview
highlights.text: Tap 1×, 2×, 3× or 4× right on the live camera.

changes: Live: one row with the live camera, the photo being analyzed (progress, or a countdown to the next photo) and the last analyzed photo
The last analyzed photo is outlined, labelled "✓ In the summary" and glows when a new one arrives
1×, 2×, 3×, 4× zoom buttons on the live preview, in sync with the zoom slider
The summary runs full width under the row
Earlier photos are small thumbnails, three to a row, without repeating the photos above
Shorter progress label (time left) so it fits the smaller tile

releases.title: See the analysis happen

highlights.title: Analysis progress
highlights.text: A ring, scan line and time-left estimate on the photo being analyzed.

highlights.title: One clear summary
highlights.text: The summary shows once, right under the photos, next to a small thumbnail.

highlights.title: Triggers at a glance
highlights.text: One line per trigger with a status badge, run count, time and a tally.

changes: Removed the separate per-photo AI summary card; the summary (with Markdown) now sits right under the live and analyzed photos
The summary's photo is a small thumbnail of the photo it was last updated from
Photo being analyzed: dimmed overlay, scan line, progress ring with percentage and a time-left estimate from recent photos, then a check mark
Compact trigger status: tally line, one line per trigger (badge, run count, last time), tap for details and the on/off switch, off triggers folded into one line
fixes: The AI summary was shown twice on the Live tab

releases.title: Send your shortcuts everything

highlights.title: Richer trigger input
highlights.text: Send the photo's summary, the reply as received or understood, or tracked details.

highlights.title: Everything as JSON
highlights.text: One JSON bundle with the trigger, photo, reply and session for your shortcut.

highlights.title: More placeholders
highlights.text: Custom messages can use {frame}, {raw}, {parsed}, {state}, {all} and more.

changes: Send to the shortcut: capture summary, photo's AI summary, reply as received, reply as understood (JSON), tracked details (JSON), everything (JSON), or a custom message

Custom-message placeholders: {summary} {frame} {raw} {parsed} {state} {all} {reason} {condition} {check} {name} {shortcut} {photo} {phototime} {time} {date} {instructions} {elapsed} {photos} {requests} {tokens} {engine}
The debug log shows exactly what each trigger sent to its shortcut

releases.title: Pause, follow along, see it drawn

highlights.title: Start, pause, stop
highlights.text: Control the session from a header that stays on top, with a countdown.

highlights.title: Visual AI summaries
highlights.text: Summaries render Markdown: tables, bar charts and gauges, in a fixed-width font.

highlights.title: Triggers tab
highlights.text: Triggers have their own tab, and every photo's AI summary sits right under it.

changes: Sticky header like Strava Daily Digest: Start, Pause/Resume, Stop, Settings, tabs, and a status line with the countdown and analyzing status
Pause stops new photos and freezes the clock and trigger timers; Resume takes a photo at once; paused time is shown separately in the report
Triggers moved to their own tab
Live: the AI summary of the latest photo right under the live and analyzed photos
Summaries, photo notes and reports render Markdown safely (no raw HTML except numeric <meter>/<progress>), in a fixed-width font
The model is told it may use Markdown, bars and gauges when the instructions ask for them
fixes: Code blocks inside a model's reply were stripped while reading it

releases.title: Watch it live, keep every session

highlights.title: Live session tab
highlights.text: See the live camera, the photo being analyzed and a countdown to the next one.

highlights.title: Sessions are saved
highlights.text: Each finished session keeps its summary, photos, triggers and debug log.

highlights.title: Report when you stop
highlights.text: End session opens a full report of everything that happened.

changes: Tabs: Setup, Live and Sessions
Live: live camera, the photo being analyzed, countdown and progress bar, zoom and End session
Ending a session collapses the page, saves the session and opens its report in Sessions
Saved session report: what happened, stats, triggers, last photos, tracked details, instructions and the debug log (Copy as JSON, Delete)
Settings › Capture: Sessions kept, 3 by default, up to 10; sessions are stored on this iPhone only

releases.title: AI settings opens on top

highlights.title: AI settings in view
highlights.text: Tapping AI settings in Settings now opens it in front, not hidden behind.

highlights.title: Back to Settings
highlights.text: Done in AI settings brings you straight back to Settings.

highlights.title: Messages you can see
highlights.text: Confirmations like Connection OK now show above Settings too.

fixes: AI settings opened behind the Settings sheet and only appeared after closing Settings
Short confirmation messages were hidden behind the Settings and AI settings sheets

releases.title: Settings, your way

highlights.title: Colours and layout
highlights.text: Six palettes or Auto, plus Compact and a Tiny layout that puts older photos on one line.

highlights.title: Text size and font
highlights.text: Pick Small to Larger text and a rounded or serif headline font.

highlights.title: One Settings screen
highlights.text: AI settings, update checks and capture limits behind the new sliders icon.

changes: New Settings sheet (sliders icon at the top): Appearance, AI, Updates with Check now, Capture tunables and Built with; changes apply at once
Appearance shared with the other apps: Auto plus six palettes (VisionX teal in all), Comfortable, Compact or Tiny layout, four text sizes, rounded or serif headlines
Tiny layout: older photos as one line each (number, time and summary); tap one to see it whole
Capture limits are adjustable with ranges and Reset: AI request time limit, photos kept on screen, photos kept in Debug
AI settings moved from the What to look for panel into Settings; the panel keeps a one-line status
Settings are saved in settings.json in iCloud Drive › Scriptable › VisionX; presets, triggers and session choices stay in vision-session.json
Built with: the blueprints this app follows, with links to read them

releases.title: Claude joins OpenAI and Apple Intelligence

highlights.title: Claude or OpenAI
highlights.text: Photo analysis, triggers and refining now work with either provider. Switch any time in AI settings.

highlights.title: Pick any model
highlights.text: Load the models your own key can use, choose one and test the connection.

highlights.title: See your token usage
highlights.text: Tokens per day, feature and model, so you always know what AI costs you.

changes: New AI settings sheet (Settings › AI settings): Claude and OpenAI keys, model picker loaded from your key, connection test, token usage per day, feature and model
Keys are entered in a native secure prompt and stored in the iOS Keychain; the page no longer receives the key at all
Photo analysis, trigger checks and instruction refining go through one shared AI call, following the app-blueprints AI configuration
No key prompt at start: Apple Intelligence works without a key, and the cloud option appears under Analyze with once a key is saved
The summary and refined instructions are labelled with the AI that wrote them
Your existing OpenAI key moves over automatically
The model is now chosen in AI settings rather than per preset; the OpenAI-only image detail setting stays
fixes: The API key was passed to the page and used for a direct-request fallback; both are gone

releases.title: Never miss an update

highlights.title: Update reminders
highlights.text: VisionX tells you when a new version is out, and waits two days if you tap Later.

highlights.title: One-tap update
highlights.text: Update right from the app. No need to run the installer again.

highlights.title: See what's new first
highlights.text: Every update shows its three best features before you install it.

changes: Update check when VisionX opens, with a what's-new sheet (Update now / Later)
Later, or tapping outside the sheet, hides the offer for two days
An offer that arrives during a capture session waits until the session ends
Version shown at the bottom of the app
releases.json, CHANGELOG.md, tools/changelog.js and docs/RELEASING.md

"What VisionX did" in the debug log for every trigger check
Hints for each run setting in the trigger editor
